header:
Date: 2027-04-22 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Daniel Wu (Redwood SE); Dr. Elena Ruiz (CISO), Tom Baxter (Head Platform), Maria Gomez (Privacy Counsel), Sanjay Iyer (Cloud Ops), Lena Park (PM)
summary: Cedarpoint Health ran through Redwood's region pinning and KMS options. Key asks: concrete sub-processor mapping for EU-only PHI, KMS custody vs envelope encryption, SSO/RBAC story, audit log retention and export for compliance, and a short benchtest for EU-region pinning and fallback. Redwood agreed to share SOC2/ISO artifacts, KMS integration docs, and to run an EU pinning bench with sample traffic.
topics: Data residency: EU-only processing and region pinning
KMS models: customer-managed vs Redwood-managed, envelope vs full custody
RBAC and SSO (SAML/OIDC) mapping for multi-tenant orgs
Audit logs, retention, and certified export for audits
transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex: All right good afternoon everyone thanks for joining. quick roll call, well capture questions as we go.
[00:00:10] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Hi this is Elena, CISO at Cedarpoint. were on a tight timeline for the assetica assessment, so focusing on EU data flows.
[00:00:22] Alex: Great, noted. Tom?
[00:00:25] Tom Baxter: Tom here. main thing for us is we cannot have PHI leave the EU jurisdiction except for encrypted backups under escrow -- long story.
[00:00:34] Priya: Thanks Tom. quick overview from our side: Redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. region pinning can be enforced at the account or route level, and we have KMS integrations for customer-managed keys. ill let Daniel zoom into the KMS shapes.
[00:00:48] Daniel: hi all. two main patterns: 1) Redwood-managed keys (we handle HSM and key rotation) which is fastest; 2) Customer-managed KMS where you hold the master key in AWS KMS / GCP KMS or bring-your-own HSM. envelope encryption is used so we never send plaintext master keys to Redwood.
[00:01:05] Maria Gomez: can you clarify envelope encryption? we need legal language for what counts as "custody" for GDPR and our auditors.
[00:01:12] Daniel: yes so plaintext master never leaves your KMS. Redwood holds data keys encrypted with your master key. when inference happens in EU region, the data key is decrypted in an ephemeral HSM or KMS call in-region. if you revoke the master key, we can't decrypt future requests.
[00:01:29] Sanjay Iyer: that sounds fine but we need proof of where the KMS calls happen. we need audit logs showing KMS key usage and the region.
[00:01:36] Priya: absolutely - we expose KMS call logs and trace IDs in our audit logs and the console. exportable JSON with timestamps, key id, request origin, and model route.
[00:01:46] Alex: can i pause for a quick qual? what infra do you run today for generative workloads? hosted endpoints, internal GPU fleet?
[00:01:54] Tom: we run a mix - mostly GCP with some on-prem for legacy apps. but this project demands EU-only processing for any patient-identifiable transcripts.
[00:02:03] Lena Park: also timeline: pilot in next 3 weeks, production Q3. success = zero-evidence-of-cross-border processing during pilot plus measurable latency under 300ms p50.
[00:02:13] Alex: good constraints, that helps. On sub-processors - we maintain a subprocessor register and can provide an in-region-only subset for EU customers. question: do you need contractual sub-processor flow-down, or technical guarantees only?
[00:02:26] Maria: both. legal wants contractual flow-down for any entity processing PHI, plus a technical attestation for in-region compute and KMS.
[00:02:34] Priya: under our enterprise DPA we can list sub-processors and do flow-downs; for EU-special cases we can carve a dedicated pool or a private deployment. the dedicated pool is physically in EU and we can limit sub-processors to partner infra providers in the EU.
[00:02:47] Dr. Elena Ruiz: how are failovers handled? if eu region goes degraded do you route to us-east automatic? thats a hard no for us.
[00:02:56] Daniel: good callout. we have configurable failover policies. default is "regional-only" for customers who enable geo-affinity. for your case we can set strict region pinning and no cross-border fallback; the trade-off is you may see request failures during capacity constraints unless you provision reserved capacity (Dedicated).
[00:03:14] Tom: reserved capacity ok but cost needs a ballpark. can you provide estimates for a 10k tokens/day workload?
[00:03:21] Alex: we'll put an initial cost estimate in the follow-up note; Priya ill loop you for sizing.
[00:03:26] Priya: noted. moving on to audit logs - what retention do you require?
[00:03:30] Maria: retention must be 7 years for some records, but for the pilot 1 year is fine; critical point is exportability and timestamp fidelity for audits.
[00:03:40] Priya: Redwood stores detailed request/response metadata for 90 days by default; enterprise plans can extend retention to configurable periods and provide export hooks to S3 in-region encrypted with your KMS.
[00:03:52] Dr. Elena Ruiz: can that export target be an EU-only bucket with keys we control?
[00:03:58] Daniel: yes - the export can be to your S3 bucket in eu-west-1 (or equivalent) and encrypted with your customer KMS key. we also provide signed manifests for tamper evidence.
[00:04:06] Sanjay: on the subprocessor list, do you use third-party telemetry or observability partners that may sample payloads?
[00:04:12] Alex: we sample telemetry but we can disable PII sampling for accounts flagged as regulated. we also offer an audited path with no payload telemetry - just metrics and traces.
[00:04:22] Maria: what about SOC2/ISO artifacts? we need the certs and the scope documents.
[00:04:26] Alex: i'll share the SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 cert PDFs and the statement of applicability; they'll be in the shared drive link after the call.
[00:04:33] Lena: can we talk about RBAC and SSO? we need SAML with SCIM provisioning and role mapping to ensure devs can't access PHI endpoints unless approved.
[00:04:41] Priya: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 and OIDC; SCIM provisioning for user sync, and per-route RBAC—roles like viewer, developer, admin, and compliance. we also support token scoping so API keys can be pinned to region and model.
[00:04:54] Tom: token scoping - how granular? can i create an API key that only allows inference in eu-west-1 and only for model-X?
[00:04:59] Daniel: yes. policy language supports region, model, route, and token expiry. theres also an endpoint-level allowlist.
[00:05:05] Maria: auditors will ask for proof of separation so please include example audit queries that show who invoked what and from where.
[00:05:12] Priya: we'll include sample queries and screenshots from the console plus the raw downloadable logs.
[00:05:18] Alex: quick micro-case: what about backups? are there cross-border backups for redundancy?
[00:05:23] Daniel: backups can be configured to be in-region only. by default, we replicate metadata for HA across regions in encrypted form, but for EU-only customers we can turn off cross-region replication. there may be a tradeoff with RTO.
[00:05:36] Dr. Elena Ruiz: okay that helps. Maria following up: legal needs the sub-processor contract wording and KMS custody language. can you do a short redline?
[00:05:44] Alex: we can provide a redline DPA template and suggested language for KMS custody and escrow.
[00:05:48] Tom: about sub-processors within EU - are there third-party model providers (e.g., partners) included in the chain?
[00:05:55] Priya: we have a model catalog. some open models we run ourselves; some partner-hosted models may be in specific regions. for EU-pinned customers we can gate the catalog to EU-hosted model variants only.
[00:06:06] Sanjay: how do you prove that inference compute never leaves EU, e.g., for auditors who ask for network diagrams?
[00:06:12] Daniel: we provide network diagrams, VPC peering maps, and signed attestations of our deployment topology. we can also provide packet flow diagrams showing egress blocked for the account.
[00:06:21] Lena: would a private deployment be simpler? were trying to avoid heavy infra ops.
[00:06:25] Alex: private on-prem is an option; it gives max control but requires your infra ops to manage nodes. dedicated hosted with reserved capacity is usually the balance—Redwood manages the infra but we carve dedicated GPU pools in-region for you.
[00:06:37] Maria: auditors will ask about key escrow — do you offer KMS escrow or key recovery?
[00:06:42] Daniel: we dont escrow customer master keys. if you choose customer-managed KMS, you keep the master. we can offer an escrow process via an authorized third-party in exceptional enterprise agreements, but that requires legal review.
[00:06:55] Tom: for the benchtest, what will be measured? we want to verify no cross-border packet and p50 latency under 300ms as said earlier. also we want to confirm KMS calls resolve in eu-west-1.
[00:07:05] Priya: proposed bench: 1) Generate synthetic traffic with PHI-like payloads from an EU egress-restricted client; 2) Pin route to EU region; 3) Enable strict failover; 4) Collect audit logs + KMS usage; 5) Verify export to your S3 with your KMS. We'll run for 48 hours.
[00:07:20] Alex: well need a test account and an S3 bucket or you can give us a pre-signed upload target. Tom?
[00:07:25] Tom: we'll stand up an EU S3 and provide credentials.
[00:07:28] Dr. Elena Ruiz: please include a list of all sub-processors touched by the bench.
[00:07:32] Alex: will do.
[00:07:35] [00:10:12] -- mid-call clarifications and brief filler --
[00:10:15] Daniel: small note on latency: deploying model-X in eu-west-1 on our dedicated pool with quantization and KV caching should meet your p50 target; we'll provide a tuning checklist.
[00:10:28] Maria: and regression alerts? we need to know if model quality degrades after a quantization or fallback.
[00:10:33] Priya: Redwood Optimize can monitor prompt sets and surface regression alerts tied to evals. we can attach your acceptance prompts and create baseline thresholds.
[00:10:42] Tom: regulator question - do you support data subject access logs? we need ability to extract per-subject processing history.
[00:10:49] Alex: we support per-customer identifiers in logs; we can include request IDs and subject tags so you can reconstruct processing flows.
[00:10:55] Sanjay: any chance of accidental metadata leaving the region via telemetry? earlier you said you can disable PII sampling - how exhaustive is that?
[00:11:03] Priya: when disabled, telemetry contains only route-level metrics and hash-only identifiers; no raw text, no user identifiers. we can also configure a hardened mode for regulated accounts.
[00:11:12] Maria: please include hardened mode checklist in the docs.
[00:11:16] Alex: noted. well include it.
[00:11:18] [00:20:00] -- longer section with details, Q&A, and a few transcription artifacts --
[00:20:05] Dr. Elena Ruiz: odd question - what if an EU customer requests data deletion? how do you certify deletion across caches, backups, and logs?
[00:20:12] Daniel: deletion: primary store deletion + key rotation for encrypted backups + purge from caches. for backups we provide a documented purge workflow and attest to completion; audit records of deletion are retained per your retention policy.
[00:20:24] Lena: what about change control for RBAC? we need approver workflows; can we integrate with our existing ticketing system?
[00:20:30] Priya: SCIM plus webhook-based approval is supported; we can integrate with Jira or ServiceNow via a small connector.
[00:20:36] Tom: okay logistics - when do we get the artifacts?
[00:20:39] Alex: i'll upload SOC2/ISO by Monday 4/25, Priya will send KMS snippets 4/26; we'll schedule bench w/c 5/3.
[00:20:46] Maria: and the DPA redline?
[00:20:48] Alex: redline DPA by 4/29.
[00:20:51] [00:30:00] -- wrap-up, recap, and closing --
[00:30:05] Alex: quick recap: 1) Redwood to provide SOC2/ISO, DPA redline, KMS integration docs; 2) Cedarpoint to send sub-processor CSV and test bucket; 3) Redwood to run 48hr EU bench with strict region pinning; 4) timeline target pilot in next 3 weeks.
[00:30:22] Dr. Elena Ruiz: that captures it. thanks everyone.
[00:30:26] Tom: thanks, appreciate it.
[00:30:29] Maria: thanks.
[00:30:31] Alex: thanks all, well follow up with links and invite for the bench kickoff.
[00:30:36] [END RECORDING at 00:52:02]
